description:
Looking for passionate teammates to build an exciting Mars exploration game!
Game designers, game developers, and UI/UX designers are highly welcome. Programmers, 3D artists, and space enthusiasts can also join. Beginners are most welcome! No experience is required—just creativity, enthusiasm, and a willingness to learn and work together. Let's turn our ideas into reality!
summary:
AREON is a first-person 3D Mars survival training game designed for children aged 7–12. Developed in Unity, it places players in Arcadia Planitia, Mars, where they undertake a three-Sol research mission as a junior astronaut.

The objective is to locate and collect three scientific data files while ensuring the astronaut survives the Martian environment. Players must monitor oxygen, power consumption, and radiation exposure, make resource-conscious exploration decisions, and return to their habitat before nightfall. The simulation incorporates real Mars environmental observations from NASA's Curiosity rover REMS instrument to provide a science-based foundation for the experience.

AREON addresses the challenge of making planetary science accessible through interactive, experience-driven learning. Rather than simply reading about Mars, players encounter its environmental constraints through gameplay, understanding why oxygen generation, energy conservation, radiation protection, and mission planning are essential for human exploration. By combining 3D simulation, resource-management mechanics, and real planetary science, AREON turns learning about Mars into an engaging astronaut training experience.
details:
Project Details – AREON: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

AREON is a first-person 3D Mars survival and exploration simulator designed for children aged 7–12. Set in Arcadia Planitia, players assume the role of a junior astronaut assigned a three-Sol scientific research mission. Their objective is to explore the Martian terrain, locate and collect three scientific data files, manage limited survival resources, and return to the habitat safely before nightfall.

The gameplay revolves around interconnected survival systems:

  • Oxygen Management: Players must monitor their oxygen supply and understand the importance of oxygen production for long-duration missions.
  • Power Management: Every action consumes energy, requiring players to balance exploration and resource conservation.
  • Radiation Protection: Players must account for radiation exposure and manage their available shielding.
  • Mission Progression: Players collect three research data files across three Sols while managing time and survival resources.
  • Habitat Safety: Returning to the habitat before nightfall is essential to completing the mission successfully.

2. Scientific Foundation and Benefits

AREON draws upon real Martian environmental observations, particularly those recorded by NASA's Curiosity rover through its Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS). These observations provide scientific context for the environmental conditions represented in the game.

The experience introduces children to important concepts in planetary science, energy conservation, astronaut safety, environmental monitoring, and mission planning. Instead of memorizing scientific facts, players learn through decisions and their consequences.

3. Technology and Development

The project is developed using:

  • Game Engine: Unity
  • Programming Language: C#
  • Development Environment: Unity Editor
  • Game Design: First-person 3D exploration and survival simulation
  • Interface: In-game HUD for monitoring survival resources and mission progress
  • Scientific Reference: NASA Mars environmental observations from the Curiosity rover REMS instrument.

The development focuses on combining 3D environments, interactive gameplay mechanics, resource-management systems, and mission progression into one cohesive experience.

4. Creativity and Innovation

The central creative idea behind AREON is that every action has a cost. Unlike conventional educational games that primarily deliver information through quizzes or static content, AREON makes players experience the constraints of surviving on Mars.

Exploration is not simply about reaching a destination; players must consider whether they have enough power, oxygen, and radiation protection to complete their objectives and return safely. This creates a decision-driven learning experience in which scientific concepts directly influence gameplay.

5. Design Considerations and Intended Impact

Our team considered the target audience's age, accessibility, gameplay simplicity, scientific relevance, and engagement. We designed the experience to make complex astronaut survival concepts understandable without requiring prior knowledge of space science. The experience is exploration-focused and combat-free, keeping the emphasis on discovery, learning, and problem-solving.

Our intended impact is to make planetary science more experiential and accessible to younger learners. AREON aims to help children understand that exploring Mars is not just about reaching another planet; it involves scientific research, resource limitations, environmental risks, and careful decision-making.
